notes.meaning: Jairus begged Jesus with deep love and urgency, calling his dying child his little daughter. He believed that if Jesus came and laid hands on her, she would recover and live. While his faith was real, he thought Jesus had to be physically present to heal her.

Jesus went with Jairus right away without turning him down. A great crowd followed along, pressing tightly against Him from every side. The crush of the crowd made it difficult to move through the streets.

A woman in the crowd had suffered from constant bleeding for twelve long years. Under Jewish law, this bleeding made her ceremonially unclean, keeping her from normal community worship and life. Her sickness had lasted just as long as Jairus’s daughter had been alive.
She had endured many painful treatments from different doctors, but none of them helped. She spent every penny she owned trying to find a cure. Instead of getting better, her illness only grew worse.

The woman had heard reports about the wonderful miracles Jesus performed for others. Shrinking from public notice because of her condition, she slipped through the thick crowd behind Him. In quiet faith, she reached out and touched His outer robe.

She kept telling herself that simply touching Jesus' clothes would be enough to cure her. She believed that touching even the edge of His garment connected her to His healing power. Her faith was bold and completely placed in Jesus.
The moment she touched His cloak, the flow of blood dried up completely. She could feel right away in her own body that the long-standing illness was gone. Her cure was instant and total.

Jesus knew within Himself at that very moment that healing power had gone out from Him. This power did not leave Him by accident, but flowed out because He willingly answered her touch of faith. He turned around in the crowd and asked who had touched His clothes.

The disciples were surprised by His question and pointed out the noisy crowd pressing against Him from all sides. To them, it seemed strange to ask who touched Him when dozens of people were bumping into Him. They did not yet understand the difference between an accidental bump and a reach of faith.

Jesus kept looking around the crowd to see the person who had reached out to Him. He already knew who she was, but He looked for her so she could step forward. He wanted her to receive a full blessing rather than slip away in secret.

The woman realized she could not stay hidden and came forward trembling with fear. She may have worried that she had broken the purity laws or taken a blessing without permission. Falling at His feet, she openly confessed the whole story of her misery and her sudden cure.

Jesus spoke to her with tender affection, calling her daughter to calm her fears. He told her that her faith in Him had healed her, and He sent her away in true peace. Her healing was now openly confirmed so she could return to community life without shame.

Messengers from Jairus’s house arrived while Jesus was still speaking and announced that the girl had died. They told the father there was no reason to trouble the Teacher anymore. To human eyes, death meant all hope was completely gone.

Jesus overheard what the messengers said and immediately spoke words of comfort to Jairus. He told the grieving father not to give in to fear, but simply to keep trusting Him. Jesus showed that death is not beyond the reach of God's power.

Jesus stopped the rest of the crowd and even most of His disciples from coming along. He permitted only Peter, James, and John to go with Him to the house. These three close disciples were chosen to be trusted eyewitnesses of what was about to happen.

When they reached the house, Jesus saw widespread confusion and loud wailing. Family members and hired mourners were crying out and making music to express their grief. This loud display confirmed how hopeless the situation seemed to everyone there.

Jesus entered the house and asked why everyone was making such a noisy scene. He told them the child was not dead, but only asleep. He called death sleep because her condition was only temporary and He was about to wake her up.

The mourners laughed at Jesus with scorn because they knew for certain that the girl was dead. Jesus sent the mockers out of the room so that only those with faith and love remained. He then took the girl's parents and His three disciples into the room where the body lay.

Jesus took the dead child gently by the hand and spoke in Aramaic, saying, Talitha koum. Mark explains that this means, Little girl, I say to you, get up. Even though touching a dead body normally made a person unclean under the law, Jesus' touch brought life instead of defilement.

The twelve-year-old girl got up immediately and began walking around the room. She was not merely revived, but completely restored to full health and strength. Everyone in the room was overcome with utter amazement at what Jesus had done.

Jesus strictly instructed the parents not to spread the news of the miracle everywhere right away. He also told them to give the girl something to eat. This practical command proved that she was truly alive in an ordinary human body, and it revealed His caring attention to her daily needs.
